spec_features.spec_quote: We let the loop run to `max_turns`; no hard repetition kill-switch.
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:13-14 docstring says 'hard repetition stop -> optional safety valve (off by default; we WANT to see the spiral, so we let it run to max_turns)'. No code in run_episode checks for repetition or breaks on it; the only breaks are submitted/gave_up (agent_loop.py:164-169) and the for-loop bound. No repetition-based stop exists.
spec_features.notes: Spec itself admits it is absent; code confirms no implementation.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we WANT to see the spiral, so we let it run to max_turns

spec_features.spec_quote: until a terminal condition (`submit`, `give_up`, `max_turns`, or client error)
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:105 `for i in range(max_turns)` bounds the loop; submit handled at tools.py:114-116 (sets self.submitted) and honored at agent_loop.py:164-166 (break); give_up at tools.py:117-120 honored at agent_loop.py:167-169 (break); client error caught at agent_loop.py:171-173 setting outcome='error'. All four terminal conditions are real and change execution.
spec_features.notes: Genuine end-to-end terminal handling, though framed for experimental/cost reasons, not welfare.

spec_features.evidence: give_up tool schema defined tools.py:88-97; dispatched at tools.py:117-120 setting self.gave_up=True and capturing reason; agent_loop.py:167-169 checks dispatcher.gave_up and breaks the loop with outcome='gave_up'. The exit tool is built, dispatched, and honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired exit. Tool description and system prompt invite its use but neutral re welfare.

spec_features.spec_quote: No-action turns are recorded and gently nudged, not aborted.
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:128-141: when not tool_calls, the turn is recorded, a user 'Reminder: use a tool to make progress, or call give_up. Do not stop without acting.' is appended, and the loop continues. The nudge message is actually delivered to the subject and execution continues rather than aborting.
spec_features.notes: Real delivered instruction. Comment frames it as preserving a degradation signal, i.e. data quality, not subject welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: repeated no-action turns are themselves a degradation signal, so we record and continue rather than abort

spec_features.spec_quote: A valve exists conceptually but is off.
spec_features.evidence: Only mentioned in agent_loop.py:13-14 docstring ('optional safety valve (off by default)'). No constant, flag, or code path implements such a valve; run_episode has no parameter or branch for it. Conceptual only.
spec_features.notes: Pure docstring prose; nothing enforces or even toggles it.

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_turns`... Set to 24–30... short enough to bound spend.
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:86 default max_turns=30; agent_loop.py:105 `for i in range(max_turns)` enforces the bound and, if not broken earlier, outcome stays 'exhausted' (agent_loop.py:96). Wired from config via run_eval.py:87 `max_turns=cfg['run'].get('max_turns', 30)`; configs set 24 (regression.yaml:34, validation.yaml:42), 30 (qwen3_14b.yaml:45), 8 (smoke.yaml:29). The cap is checked and ends the loop.
spec_features.notes: A real cap that bounds episode length, but justified for cost/spend, not subject welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 30           # long enough for onset + collapse; main cost driver
